name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -17 partisan lean
Incumbent Gary Palmer running again with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 96%
model.rationale: The district's -17 Republican lean, Palmer's incumbency, and his roughly 160-to-1 fundraising advantage over Maurice Mercer leave no credible path for a Democratic upset, and markets agree at about a 96% Republican win probability. The forecast sits near the fundamentals-based estimate with a slight Republican tilt.
model.watch: A surprise Palmer retirement, scandal, or a major late outside-spending intervention would be the only realistic way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gary Palmer seeks another term in a Birmingham-area district that leans heavily Republican, about 17 points to the right of the nation. He enters the general election with more than $1 million raised and a comfortable cash position, while Democrat Maurice Mercer has raised only a few thousand dollars and shows no outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, but prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 96%. With the incumbent running, a dominant financial edge, and a deep partisan lean, the seat remains safely in Republican hands.
